methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $305M total raised proxy.

private.name: ICON
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series C)

data.narrative:
Meter is a Series C-stage housing and construction company founded by Anil and Sunil Varanasi. The valuation analysis draws on a limited comparable universe: one private peer (ICON) and no public comparables in the construction technology space, reflecting both sector fragmentation and the early-stage nature of frontier technology in housing.

The stage-progression method was applied as the primary triangulation approach. Using Meter's $305M in total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression to later stages yields an implied valuation of $518M. This method is grounded in observed funding step-ups within venture stages but relies on the assumption that capital raised correlates meaningfully to value creation at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $441M to $596M, with $518M as the median point. However, this range reflects limited input: only one applicable valuation method and a thin comparable set. The key uncertainties are material. The lack of public market comparables precludes revenue multiple or profitability benchmarking. The single private comparable provides limited triangulation power. Confidence in this range is therefore moderate and contingent on deeper commercial diligence around unit economics, market TAM validation, and competitive positioning relative to ICON and other unlisted peers.
